text:
maya: Heads up — NA-east hotpool saturating, dequeue latency spiking ~100-200ms for short prompts. Noticing high KV cache miss & batching spinups around 2067890000.

diego: seeing it too, dashboards show hotpool GPU util ~98% and queue depth up. 

liam: linking traces, looks like continuous-batcher commit a3f4b2 pushed last night changed target batch window, causing many small batches to form and KV cache thrash.

maya: @diego can you throttle new hotpool allocations and stop autoscale for NA-east while we triage?

diego: done — triggered `./infra scale hotpool na-east --action pause-autoscale` at 2067890145. infra-bot: autoscale paused for hotpool na-east by diego.

alex: pushing a quick filter on routing — divert 30% traffic from na-east hotpool to dedicated-pools (na-dedicated-1/2). command: `routectl set-policy --region na-east --divert 30% --targets dedicated`

ops-bot: routing policy updated: na-east -> {dedicated:30%, hotpool:70%}.

liam: I'm preparing a rollback of the continuous-batcher change. Recommend revert to 63f9d8 and re-deploy to runtime-nodes in hotpool. Will take ~6-8min to rollout.

maya: before rollback, can we try KV-prefill and bump KV cache TTL to reduce misses? Quick patch: `kvctl set-ttl --pool hotpool --ttl 600s` and `kvctl prewarm --prefix user:recent`

liam: applied ttl bump at 2067890250. Prewarm started — ~45% of active keys warmed so far.

sre-oncall: traffic shift helped — p50 latency down 30ms, p95 still high. Need to be careful with cost if dedicated pools keep absorbing load.

diego: spun up 2 emergency GPU nodes in na-east hotpool (ephemeral) to relieve backpressure: `provisioner create --type a100 --count 2 --ephemeral` at 2067890328. infra-bot: 2 nodes provisioning.

ops-bot: cost alert muted for emergency provision for 2 hours by diego.

liam: rollback started at 2067890345 — deploying 63f9d8 to runtime image tag `runtime:v63f9d8-rollback`. Will verify batch metrics post-rollout.

maya: logs show KV miss rate dropping since TTL bump and prewarm — good sign. Keep an eye on tail latency.

liam: rollback complete at 2067890410. batch size distribution back to baseline, batch count per-second dropped ~40% on hotpool.

sre-oncall: p95 latency reduced to near-normal within 2 minutes of rollback. Monitoring for 30min.

alex: leaving routing divert in place for an hour to avoid reloading hotpool.

diego: autoscale remains paused; created a follow-up task to run canary for new batcher config in a staging region before re-enabling: TICKET-6543.

maya: great work — postmortem notes: 1) bad default batch window increased small-batch churn 2) KV prewarm should be part of deploy for hotpools 3) emergency provision playbook needs clearer cost knobs.

liam: I'll open PR for canary pipeline + add automated KV prewarm step.

sre-oncall: closing incident channel after 30m of stable metrics. If anyone sees regressions ping here. :thumbsup:
